chapter: Working with Coleman and Smiling Joe
title: Freddie Coleman's band at the Mardi Gras lounge and its records
summary: Looking at a photo of the Mardi Gras employees, they identify band members and discuss the records the band made.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: What was your main job then after that? You said that Freddie Coleman, you went with him.
Yeah, I went with Freddie Coleman.
The bunch was in the picture, mostly. Yeah. So you all was there. Tourmalon played with him for a while, didn't he?

Yeah, Tourmalon was with us. He was playing bass, wasn't he? He was playing bass. Well, during that time, I was at the Matty Grind, and this is all the employees here, Joe Robichore. He was playing intermissions. Oh yeah.

Yeah, Joe Robichore and Lindsey Miles. I see, who else? That Lindsey Miles there, there's Joe Robichore sitting beside me at the piano. That one big picture they're taking, all the employees. Let's go from left to right.
That was the bar, that's Cindy Davila. Oh yeah, Cindy Davila.

And the trombone behind him? Oh, Wendell Eugene. And there's Willie Humphrey. Willie Humphrey. And this is Lizzie. Lizzie. And who's this on trumpet? Talking about Jefferson. Oh yeah, Thomas Jefferson. That's Thomas Jefferson. That was a wild one.
That's Frederick Coleman himself. And who's on bass? And that's Clement. Clement Camelot. Oh, Clement. He wasn't as heavy then.
Couldn't recognize him hardly. He's pretty light weight.
Yeah, I think that was a nice summer. And Willie Humphrey. And Willie Humphrey. Yeah. Frog was with you there for a while though too. The records they made, I think he...
Frog came there after Wendell left. See, Wendell on Tramble on that night.
After Wendell left and Frog came. Those records that Cook, a fellow from Long Island made, were you on those? I never did have those. They were cut out.

Well, I was on a lot of records. Fred had made a lot of records. Yeah, we did record. And I was wrong, because he's always loved me to try to find it. I still can't find any. I never did hear those records myself. I had them once.
I had Willie Humphrey. Willie Humphrey, somebody bought a copy of it. That's the last copy I ever got. And they didn't have a distributor.
I think the company is perfectly out of business now. At least you can't get that record. I don't know what happened.
